full_judgment: 6. It further appears that though the respondents persistently claimed that the whereabouts of Jainab Khatun were not known and the petitioners claim was based on documents which were not genuine but still no attempt was ever made by the petitioners to produce the aforesaid Jainab Khatun before the Court of settlement to prove the bonafide character of their documents. It is strange to note that the deed of agreement alleged to have been executed on 20.08.1970 in favour of Mrs. Sahera Rashid was not produced before the Court of Settlement but it has been annexed before the High Court Division and in the said document it appears that consideration was fixed at Tk.40,000/- out of which Tk.35,000/- is said to have been paid at the time of execution of the agreement as earnest money and only Tk.5,000/- was left to be paid before registration. The learned Advocate-on-Record failed to reply as to what was the necessity for appointing an attorney by Mrs. Jainab Khatun on 03.05.1972 for execution of the deed of sale in favour of Mrs. Sahera Rashid though the deed of sale itself was registered about two and a half months thereafter on 15.07.1972. Non-production of original documents before the Court of Settlement along with failure to produce Mrs. Jainab Khatun casts doubt as to the genuineness of the claim of the petitioners. The property being declared as abandoned property the onus lay on the shoulder of the petitioners to rebut the presumption of correctness in enlisting the property as abandoned property. In view of the discussion made above it appears that the petitioners failed to discharge the onus and hence the High Court Division correctly discharged the rule.
